title: First 5 Minutes — Success Paths and Fallbacks (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This note captures a compact, operational plan for the "first 5 minutes" experience when a developer tries Redwood SDK for the first time (CLI or language client). Goal: 95% of new flows should see a meaningful success signal within 5 minutes (hello-world response, embedder test, or a streamed token), and we should have clear, actionable fallbacks for the remaining 5%. This is intentionally narrow — we want reproducible success heuristics that can be validated by telemetry and a small set of automated smoke checks.

Context / why this doc exists:
- We ship a lot of onboarding assets (quickstarts, samples, SDKs) but we don’t have a concise operational checklist that ties UX, telemetry, and automated recovery together.
- This doc focuses on the minimal happy path + 3 common fail modes + immediate recovery options so solutions eng and docs can align on the minimal set of diagnostics and runbooks.
- Related: ENG-9421 (cli-first failure modes), DOCS-210 (quickstart rewrite), PR #834 adds a lightweight smoke-run command to sdk-cli.

Success metrics (how we'll measure):
- Time-to-first-success (TTFS) median <= 90s for interactive flows, 95th percentile <= 240s.
- First-attempt success rate >= 95% for new users using the guided quickstart.
- For failures, 80% of cases fall into one of the predefined fail-mode buckets and display a targeted remediation hint.
- Runbook coverage: every fail mode has a single-step actionable suggestion surfaced to user (CLI error text, docs anchor) and a telemetry event emitted.

Minimal happy paths to cover (prioritized):
1) CLI quickstart: user runs `rwd login` -> `rwd demo hello` -> sees streamed response.
2) Node client: `npm init` small snippet -> call text.generate -> gets OK response.
3) Embedder smoke: small README snippet that computes similarity of two strings and returns a score.
4) Local network simulation: emulate poor connectivity and show graceful retry/backoff behavior.

Observed common failure modes (source: internal SRE + solutions notes):
A) Missing API key / bad credentials (most common)
B) Network egress blocked or corporate proxy
C) Version mismatch (client binary too old for server-side contract / field names changed)
D) Quota / billing block or geographic region mismatch (model not available)
E) TLS / certificate issues (private deployments)

For each fail mode: what the user sees -> quick remediation -> telemetry event to emit
- A) Missing API key: CLI prints `no API key found` with `rwd login --help` hint. Remediation: `rwd login` flow or set REDWOOD_API_KEY env var. Telemetry: onboarding.fail.missing_key with step=login_attempt.
- B) Network/proxy: SDK times out with socket error. Remediation: show `--offline-check` suggestion linking to troubleshooting page + sample curl test. Telemetry: onboarding.fail.network with traces.
- C) Version mismatch: error includes required minimum client version. Remediation: `npm i @redwood/sdk@latest` or `rwd upgrade`. Telemetry: onboarding.fail.version.
- D) Quota/billing: HTTP 402/403 variant. Remediation: link to billing console and show `rwd status --subscription`. Telemetry: onboarding.fail.billing.
- E) TLS/private: explicit certificate error with a pointer to internal ops guide for Private customers. Telemetry: onboarding.fail.tls.

Instrumentation plan (minimal events & labels):
- onboarding.attempt.start (flow=cli|node|python|embed, experiment=oneclick-v2, user_type=trial|paid)
- onboarding.step.complete (step=login|hello_response|embed_check)
- onboarding.fail (fail_mode=missing_key|network|version|billing|tls, error_code, duration_s)
- onboarding.recovery.attempt (action=retry|upgrade|set_key|open_billing)
- onboarding.heatmap.{step} (counts per minute for dashboarding)

Telemetry privacy note: no prompt contents should be logged. Only metadata, error codes, and duration. Work with privacy/legal on a single telemetry schema PR before shipping.

Quick CLI scripts / smoke commands for engineering labs (draft):
- `rwd smoke hello --expect-stream` : runs a 3-step smoke connect -> model ping -> stream tokens. Returns 0 on success, 2 on recoverable error.
- `rwd smoke embed --a "foo" --b "bar"` : computes embedding similarity and returns numeric score. Failures print a checker URL for debug.
- `rwd check env` : verifies REDWOOD_API_KEY, reachable endpoint, TLS handshake, and outputs compact diagnostics for copy/paste into support tickets.

Guided UX copy (short, to be used in CLI and docs):
- Successful hello: "All set — you received 3 tokens in 0.7s. Try `rwd demo chat` next to see streaming."
- Missing key: "No API key detected. Run `rwd login` or set REDWOOD_API_KEY. If you expected a key from your org, check channel #platform-oncall."
- Network: "Connection timed out. Run `curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/health` — if you're behind a proxy, see docs: <confluence link>."

Heatmap & session tracing (visualization idea):
- Lightweight heatmap that shows drop-off by minute for first 10 minutes of the flow. Add a filter for sample size and for new vs returning users.
- Trace link pattern: onboarding.trace_id -> link to a small trace viewer with request/response durations, retries, and the emitted onboarding telemetry events.

Small experiment matrix (A/B candidates):
- A1: Inline remediation hints in CLI error output (short) vs A2: just provide a one-line error + `rwd check env` suggestion.
- B1: Auto-open browser to docs after success vs B2: do not.
- C1: Offer `rwd demo auto-fallback` which tries a cheaper quantized model if the preferred model not available.

Open questions / risks:
- How noisy will onboarding telemetry be? We need sampling strategy for free-tier traffic. (Action: SRE to propose sampling; ticket: ENG-9503)
- For Private installs, telemetry may be disabled. We must ensure in-doc runbook covers offline troubleshooting fully.
- UX trade: do we block on `rwd login` or allow tokenless demo limited to public sample models? (Security input required)

Immediate next steps (owners & rough ETA):
- Jordan: land minimal telemetry schema + sample events (PR to instrumentation repo) — ETA 2025-10-10.
- Marissa: update quickstart docs with the new CLI copy examples and embed smoke snippets — ETA 2025-10-07.
- Samir: add `rwd smoke hello` to CLI PR #834 and wire exit codes — ETA 2025-10-03 (working).
- Eliot: design heatmap mock and add to Redwood Console backlog as a new card — ETA 2025-10-15.

Risks / notes to self:
- Keep the CLI error strings stable (tests depend on exact phrases) — coordinate with QA before changing wording.
- Make the `rwd check env` output copy-paste friendly for support tickets (include short diagnostic id).

Appendix: example CLI session transcript (simulated)
$ rwd demo hello
> detecting credentials... none found
> No API key detected. Run `rwd login` or set REDWOOD_API_KEY. For SSO users see https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DX/SSO+onboarding
$ rwd login
> browser opened to login.redwood.ai
> done — API key stored in credentials store
$ rwd demo hello
> connected to model: redwood/ggml-mini-v1
> streaming: "Hello from Redwood!"

Last notes: aim to keep this tight. If we can get the CLI smoke commands and telemetry schema landed this sprint, we can instrument a small study of <500 new signups and validate the TTFS target. Will iterate after we collect one week's worth of telemetry.
